records.description: An offer with affiliateUrl explicitly null. This is the truthful, common case: no attribution mechanism exists in source (AFFILIATE_AUTHORITY: ABSENT), so 'no attribution' must remain 'no attribution' rather than being backfilled with anything.
records.notes: data/catalog.json: every one of ~60 real fixture entries has affiliateUrl: null. No affiliate ID, click ID, or network ID minting exists anywhere in source (grep for affiliateId|clickId|trackingId|networkId|utm_|partnerId returns zero hits).

records.description: A candidate affiliateUrl carries embedded basic-auth-style credentials. This must be rejected as a destination outright — attribution safety checking is a URL-safety problem, not a URL-rewriting problem, and this corpus does not invent a scrubbing mechanism that doesn't exist in source.
records.notes: services/commerceDestination.ts:56-69 isSafeCommerceUrl rejects any URL with parsed.username/password set, regardless of which field (productUrl vs affiliateUrl) carried it — commerceDestination.ts treats affiliateUrl as just another untrusted candidate URL.

records.description: A URL carries an ordinary-looking UTM/tracking query string that the PROVIDER supplied. This must not be interpreted as governed K Scan attribution (since none exists) — it is preserved as part of the URL, but the corpus must not label it 'K Scan attribution' or assert revenue tracking is occurring.
records.notes: commerceDestination.ts does not inspect, strip, or interpret query strings at all (only protocol/credentials/host) — a tracking parameter passes through unexamined. This corpus must not claim it represents K Scan-operated affiliate attribution, since AFFILIATE_AUTHORITY: ABSENT.

records.description: An ordinary, non-tracking query parameter (e.g. a color/size selector) on a retailer URL must be preserved untouched when selecting the Shop destination.
records.notes: services/commerceDestination.ts:77-85 selectCommerceDestination returns the URL text unmodified; no parameter stripping/rewriting occurs for safe URLs.

records.description: A safe-looking https redirect URL through a third-party redirect host is a URL-safety case, not an attribution case: it may be opened if it passes isSafeCommerceUrl, but that alone must never be presented as proof of governed affiliate attribution.
records.notes: Overlaps with dom-affiliate-redirect-domain in domains/domain-resolution.json by design: the same URL shape is both a domain-truth case (retailer identity) and an attribution case (no governed program exists to have produced this redirect).

records.description: A bare canonical merchant URL with no query string at all is the simplest true case: no attribution, no tracking, nothing to preserve or strip.
records.notes: Baseline case for the attribution category.
